_about: Accepted npm audit findings for web/, read by tools/npm-audit-gate.py.
An entry suppresses exactly one advisory ID and nothing else — a new advisory on the
same package still fails the build. Every entry carries a reason and a review_by date,
and the gate FAILS once review_by has passed, so an exception cannot quietly become
permanent. Adding an entry is a security decision (NFR-4): record why the vulnerable
code path is not reachable, not merely that the fix is inconvenient.

accepted.reason: RSC-mode CSRF bypass: an action can run before the framework returns 400. SpanSight's SPA uses react-router in client-side mode only — BrowserRouter with Routes/Route, plus useNavigate/useParams/NavLink. It declares no RSC route modules, no server actions and no react-router server runtime, and the SPA is served as static files by Azure Static Web Apps against a separate .NET API, so the vulnerable request path does not exist in this deployment.
accepted.fix: Upgrade react-router-dom to >=8.3.0. No 7.x patch exists (7.x ends at 7.18.1), so this is a major-version migration: tracked separately, and it needs the Playwright + axe suites re-run before merge.
